# Lisbon 5-Day Plan for 2 Adults

A moderate-pace Lisbon trip that stays within your comfort rules: no starts before 09:00, one museum max per day, food-market focus, and one seafood dinner. I’m assuming a mid-range stay with breakfast included and a centrally located hotel under 140 EUR per night.

## Day-by-Day Lisbon Timeline

Day 1: Baixa + Chiado arrival day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- 09:30: Check in or drop bags, then coffee near Rossio.
- 11:00: Walk Praça do Comércio, Rua Augusta, and Baixa’s grid streets.
- 13:00: Lunch at a classic tascas-style spot or market hall.
- 15:00: Explore Chiado shops and viewpoints at a relaxed pace.
- 19:30: Easy dinner in the center; keep it light after travel.

Day 2: Alfama + Castelo + seafood dinner
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- 09:30: Start in Alfama before the crowds build.
- 11:00: Visit São Jorge Castle area and nearby miradouros.
- 13:00: Lunch in Alfama with simple grilled fish or petiscos.
- 15:00: Slow walk through narrow lanes, tiles, and viewpoints.
- 20:00: Seafood dinner in Cais do Sodré or near the river.

Day 3: Mercado da Ribeira + Bairro Alto + museum
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg
- 09:30: Late breakfast, then head to Time Out Market / Mercado da Ribeira.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/8/83/Lobster%2C_Time_Out_Market_Lisboa_%2850661858143%29.jpg Alt=09:30: Late breakfast, then head to Time Out Market / Mercado da Ribeira, Lisbon, Portugal
- 11:30: Browse market stalls and sample local bites.
- 14:00: One museum visit only: choose Museu Nacional do Azulejo or MAAT.
- 16:30: Rest break or café stop.
- 19:30: Dinner in Bairro Alto, then a gentle evening stroll.

Day 4: Belém historic day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg
- 09:30: Leave for Belém after breakfast.
- 10:00: Jerónimos Monastery exterior and Belém riverside walk.
- 12:00: Pastéis de Belém stop.
- 13:30: Lunch near the river or market-style casual dining.
- 15:00: Choose one museum or monument interior only if energy allows.
- 18:30: Return to center for a relaxed dinner.

Day 5: Markets + viewpoints + departure buffer
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/map.svg
- 09:30: Final breakfast and check-out logistics.
- 11:00: Feira da Ladra if it’s a Tuesday or Saturday; otherwise a neighborhood market.
- 13:00: Last lunch in a scenic district like Graça or Príncipe Real.
- 15:00: Souvenir stop and viewpoint time.
- 18:00: Head to the airport with a cushion for transit.

## Budget Breakdown for 5 Days

| Category | Target | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Hotel | EUR 560–700 | 4 nights under 140 EUR/night, breakfast included |
| Food & drinks | EUR 420–520 | Markets, casual lunches, 1 seafood dinner |
| Local transport | EUR 60–90 | Metro, tram, occasional taxi |
| Attractions | EUR 120–180 | Castles, one museum/day max, select entries |
| Snacks / coffee / extras | EUR 100–140 | Pasteis, drinks, small treats |
| Buffer | EUR 150–220 | Flex for upgrades or transit changes |

**Estimated total:** **EUR 1,410–1,850**

Best-fit target to stay inside your budget: **EUR 1,650–1,750**. That leaves room for a comfortable hotel while keeping the trip relaxed.

## Neighborhoods to Prioritize in Lisbon

Option 1: Baixa
A practical base for first-time visitors, easy transit, and flat walking.
Key fit: central, convenient, good for gentle pacing.

Option 2: Chiado
Best for cafés, shopping, and easy access to historic areas.
Key fit: balanced atmosphere, walkable, strong dining options.

Option 3: Alfama edge
Best for atmosphere and historic charm without being too far from the center.
Key fit: scenic, traditional, close to viewpoints.

Option 4: Cais do Sodré
Best for market access and riverfront dining.
Key fit: ideal for food-focused evenings and transit.

Option 5: Príncipe Real
Best for quieter streets, good restaurants, and a polished neighborhood feel.
Key fit: comfortable base with solid food options.
